title: Patched modules and density in local deformation rings
summary: Build arithmetic component detection for the general GL_d(F) patched module and deduce faithfulness of its unrestricted framed local deformation action. From this obtain Zariski density of crystalline lifts with regular weights varying, potentially crystabelline lifts with one regular weight fixed, and unramified degree-d induced supercuspidal lifts with that weight fixed. Further endpoints are benign density, density for every prescribed inertial type with varying regular weights, and fixed-weight minimal-stratum density. The patched results assume p∤2d.

targets.name: Potentially semistable point sets
targets.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite, d≥1, L/ℚ_p a sufficiently large finite coefficient field with integers O and residue k, and ρ̄:G_F→GL_d(k) continuous, with absolutely irreducible Jordan–Hölder factors after the allowed coefficient enlargement. Put R=R□_{ρ̄} and X=Spec R. Points mean kernels of O-algebra maps R→L′ for finite L′/L, equivalently closed points of Spec R[1/p], mapped into X. Label Hodge–Tate weights decreasingly, k_{σ,1}>⋯>k_{σ,d}; use HT(ε)=−1. Σcris consists of crystalline points of any regular labelled weight. Σ_k consists of potentially semistable points of the fixed regular weight k. Σprnc_k is its potentially crystabelline subset (crystalline after a finite abelian extension). Σspcd_k consists of those x∈Σ_k with N=0 and WD(ρ_x) irreducible, induced from a character of the Weil group of the unramified degree-d extension. Local Langlands uses CEGGPS r_p(π)=rec_p(π⊗|det|^{(1−d)/2}), with geometric Artin reciprocity. The algebraic test representation is πalg(ρ)=L_a^d⊗L for a_{σ,i}=k_{σ,i}−(d−i); thus its highest weight is −a_{σ,d+1−i}.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: Use the local lifting-ring point functor, then define the subsets by the stated p-adic Hodge and Weil–Deligne conditions. Read weights through CEGGPS §1.8: the lattice L_a is dualised in πalg. Compare DPS Remark 5.14 only after reversing its HT(ε)=+1 convention. Factor out embeddings of residue fields: changing a field of definition preserves the underlying prime and the predicates.

api.statement: A finite coefficient extension carries each of the three sets to the corresponding base-changed set and preserves its point predicate.

For x∈Σprnc_k, the Frobenius-semisimplified Weil–Deligne representation has N=0 and is a direct sum of characters of W_F. Under the normalized local Langlands correspondence its smooth representation has principal-series cuspidal support; the full induced principal series need not be irreducible.
An irreducible induced Weil representation in Σspcd_k has N=0 and corresponds to a supercuspidal representation.
The ordered weights k correspond to the dual of L_a, with a_{σ,i}=k_{σ,i}−(d−i).
Every arithmetic point avoids p and has residue field finite over L.

locator.where: BIP §6, p. 46, definitions preceding Theorem 6.1; CEGGPS §1.8, pp. 12–15; DPS Remark 5.14, p. 38; BIP lines 2286–2312; CEGGPS lines 460–535; DPS lines 1742–1765

tests.statement: For d=1, regularity is vacuous; the unramified degree-one extension is F itself, so Σspcd_k=Σprnc_k=Σ_k.
A semistable noncrystalline two-dimensional representation with N≠0 is in Σ_k for its regular weights but is in neither Σprnc_k nor Σspcd_k.
For d=2 and weights (1,0) at each embedding, the test algebraic representation has highest weight (0,0).
Two maps into finite extensions differing by a coefficient-field embedding define the same point and the same membership predicates.
For d=2 and weights (2,0), a=(1,0) and the dual highest weight is (0,−1); using (1,0) would fail the dual convention.

targets.name: Potentially diagonalizable lift input
targets.statement: For every ρ̄ in the standing setup, use the crystalline regular potentially diagonalizable lift supplied by gap:pd-crystalline-lift after finite coefficient extension. For p∤2d this discharges the lift hypothesis in CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility §5.1, so its general patched-module construction applies to arbitrary ρ̄, subject to that section’s globalisation contracts.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: Apply ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions §2.1 together with gap:pd-crystalline-lift, then import the parent §5.1 construction with its own globalisation hypotheses and suppliers. Finite coefficient extensions are faithfully flat, so a zero local annihilator and the resulting density descend to O.

locator.where: EG Theorem 1.2.2, p. 3; Definition 6.4.2 and Theorem 6.4.4, pp. 168–169; BIP §6, p. 46, paragraph before Lemma 6.3; EG lines 193–200, 6961–6965; BIP lines 2329–2335

tests.statement: For d=1, a crystalline character is already diagonalizable: the direct-sum comparison has one summand.
For a semisimple residual representation, CEGGPS Lemma 2.2 supplies regular induced-character lifts; this agrees with the universal lift contract.
At p=d=3 the lift contract still applies, but p divides 2d=6 and the patched density conclusion is outside the theorem.

targets.name: Patched deformation components
targets.statement: For the imported CEGGPS module and ring, R∞≅R□_{ρ̄}⊗̂_O A as R□_{ρ̄}-algebras, with A complete local noetherian, O-flat, reduced and equidimensional. Hence R∞ is reduced, O-flat and flat over R□_{ρ̄}. After finite coefficient enlargement making each A/𝔭 geometrically integral, its minimal primes are indexed bijectively by (χ,𝔭), where χ:μ_{p∞}(F)→O× and 𝔭∈Min(A). The associated component ring is R□,χ_{ρ̄}⊗̂_O A/𝔭; distinct pairs are distinct and contraction to R□_{ρ̄} is its χ-component prime. Here R□,χ fixes the determinant on μ_{p∞}(F), not the whole determinant.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: Separate the selected p-place factor from the auxiliary local factors in the parent construction; absorb formally smooth variables in A. Apply the gap:completed-tensor-reduced-equidimensional and gap:geometric-component-splitting interfaces to auxiliary Kisin rings. Import the BIP determinant-torsion component theorem from the local-ring owner. Geometric integrality identifies exactly the pairs of minimal primes under completed tensor product.

locator.where: BIP Lemma 6.3, p. 47; Corollaries 4.19, 4.21–4.22 as supplier inputs; BIP lines 2339–2360; CEGGPS lines 3304–3324; HP lines 2680–2759

tests.statement: When A is geometrically integral there is one patched component over each χ.
For A=O[[x]]/(x²−ϖ), A is a domain but after adjoining a root a²=ϖ it has two minimal primes (x−a) and (x+a); there are then two components over each χ.
For A=O[[u,v]]/(uv), the two minimal-prime quotients O[[u]] and O[[v]] remain integral after coefficient extension, giving two components over each χ.
Fixing χ does not fix the unramified determinant: in rank one over ℚ_p the unramified parameter remains a free variable.

targets.name: Roots of torsion-free characters
targets.statement: If ψ:G_F→O× is continuous and trivial on the torsion subgroup of G_F^ab, then for every integer d≥1 there is, after a finite extension L′/L, a continuous η:G_F→O_{L′}× with η^d=ψ. No assumption p∤2d is used in this lemma.
hypotheses: F/ℚ_p finite; d≥1; ψ continuous and trivial on torsion.
targets.proofSketch: Use the torsion-free quotient G_F^ab/tors≅Ẑ×ℤ_p^{[F:ℚ_p]}. Split off an unramified Teichmüller character whose d-th power matches the residue on the Ẑ generator. The remaining character factors through ℤ_p^{[F:ℚ_p]+1} with principal-unit values. Choose finitely many d-th roots 1+y_i after one finite coefficient extension, and use the convergent binomial powers (1+y_i)^x for x∈ℤ_p. Multiply by the Teichmüller root and inflate. The torsion hypothesis is what makes the quotient construction possible.

locator.where: BIP Lemma 6.4, p. 47; BIP lines 2364–2378

tests.statement: For d=1 the root is η=ψ.
On a torsion-free ℤ_p generator γ with ψ(γ)=1+p, adjoining a root b with b^p=1+p gives η(γ)=b even for d=p; the convergent binomial powers extend η to ℤ_p.
For F=ℚ_3 and d=2, a character taking the order-two torsion element to −1 has no square root on that element: η(t)²=1 must hold, contrary to ψ(t)=−1.

targets.name: Algebraic central character
targets.statement: Let ψ:G_F→O× be a crystalline lift of detρ̄ and xψ:R_{detρ̄}→O. On Mψ=M∞⊗̂_{R_{detρ̄},xψ}O, the centre acts by δ^{-1}, where δ=(ε^{d(d−1)/2}ψ)∘Art_F for geometric Art_F. The parent supplies that Mψ is nonzero projective in the compact fixed-central-character category. The restriction δ|_{Z∩K}, identified on O_F×, is the evaluation of an algebraic character θ of (Res_{F/ℚ_p}G_m)_L. The sign of θ is obtained by converting the arithmetic reciprocity convention of PadicHodgeTheory §3.6 to geometric reciprocity.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: Use parent central projectivity, CEGGPS §4.22 and Corollary 4.26; do not reconstruct the fixed-centre module. The product ε^{d(d−1)/2}ψ is crystalline. Apply the rank-one crystalline classification to its restriction through the geometric Artin map, obtained by inversion from the supplied arithmetic map. The algebraic exponents determine θ. Keep the inverse on Mψ and δ on its contragredient Banach dual.

locator.where: BIP Lemma 6.6, p. 48; CEGGPS §4.22 and Corollary 4.26, pp. 67–70; BIP lines 2396–2412

tests.statement: For d=1 and ψ=1, the exponent d(d−1)/2 is 0, so δ=1.
For d=2, F=ℚ_5, ψ=1 and u=2, geometric Artin gives δ(2)=2; arithmetic Artin would give 1/2.
With δ(2)=2, the compact central action is 1/2 and the contragredient action on a functional is 2, since (2·f)(m)=f(2⁻¹·m)=2f(m).

targets.name: Capture and scalar actions
targets.statement: Import capture and algebraic capture from CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility §5.3 via gap:algebraic-capture. For compact H with an open pro-p subgroup, a family (V_i) captures a compact pseudo-compact O[[H]]-module M precisely when the common kernel of all continuous equivariant maps M→V_i* is zero. If a commuting scalar kills every test, it kills M; when the R-action on M is faithful it is zero. This scalar consequence is used on the actual M∞ testing modules.
hypotheses: H compact with an open pro-p subgroup, M pseudo-compact, tests finite-dimensional continuous; commuting R-action, faithful only for the zero-scalar consequence.
targets.proofSketch: A vector in the image of an endomorphism killed by every testing map belongs to their common kernel, hence is zero. Apply this to scalar endomorphisms. Algebraically the same calculation uses Submodule.mem_iInf, LinearMap.mem_ker and Module.annihilator_eq_bot; it is a consequence of the supplied kernel and annihilator APIs.

locator.where: EP Definition 2.1 and Lemmas 2.2–2.8, pp. 342–344; EP lines 266–354, 612–621

tests.statement: For H={1}, the trivial representation L captures M=O, since the inclusion O→L has zero kernel.
The empty family captures M exactly when M=0; its common kernel is M.
For M=O/ϖ≠0 all maps to every V_i* vanish, so even the family of all characteristic-zero representations fails to capture M.
For a cyclic group H of order prime to p and a nontrivial O-valued character χ, the trivial representation alone does not capture the rank-one compact module O(χ).
For R=ℤ/4 acting on M=ℤ/2, the nonzero scalar 2 kills M; only zero action, rather than zero scalar, follows without faithfulness.
For H={1}, M=O and W=0, the tensor test family has common kernel O≠0; W≠0 is required in tensor stability.

targets.name: Patched testing modules
targets.statement: For a compact open H⊆K, finite-dimensional continuous H-representation V over L and H-stable O-lattice Θ, extend the parent testing construction to M∞,H(Θ)=(Hom_cont,O[[H]](M∞,Θ^d))^d, using Schikhof duals. This is a finite R∞-module. Its rational version M∞,H(V)=M∞,H(Θ)[1/p] is canonically independent of Θ. It is contravariantly tested against V* and its continuous L-linear dual is Hom_H(V,Π(M∞)); scalar actions are by precomposition. For σ=πalg(k)⊗σ(τ) at H=K this is the existing parent type-specialised module, not a new type-theory object.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: Restrict the finite R∞[[K]] presentation to H, which has finite index, so it remains finite over R∞[[H]]. The right action on Θ is v·g=g⁻¹v. Identify the displayed double dual with the completed balanced tensor Θ⊗̂_{O[[H]]}M∞. A finite presentation makes it a quotient of finitely many copies of R∞⊗_OΘ, proving finiteness. Compare commensurable lattices after inverting p and use torsion-free biduality for the Hom adjunction. Frobenius reciprocity compares H-tests with induced K-tests. Use the imported parent theorem, rather than general finiteness, to obtain reduced O-flat faithful quotients for algebraic and type-specialised tests.

api.statement: Two stable lattices give canonically isomorphic rational testing modules, compatibly with third-lattice comparison.
The continuous rational dual identifies with Hom_H(V,Π(M∞)), respecting R∞ actions.
Finite direct sums of V give the corresponding direct sums of testing modules.
A scalar a acts trivially on the testing module exactly when precomposition by a kills every continuous H-map M∞→V*.
For finite-index H⊆K, testing V on H agrees with testing Ind_H^K V on K, by the finite-index Frobenius adjunction.
For the finite integral test, nonzero characteristic-zero fibre at y is equivalent to a nonzero V-map into Π_y; coefficient extension to κ(y) is understood.
At H=K and V=πalg(k)⊗σ(τ), this construction agrees canonically with CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility §5.2.

locator.where: BIP §6, p. 48, paragraphs after Lemma 6.6; EP proof of Proposition 2.11, p. 345; Theorem 5.3, pp. 364–365; CEGGPS §1.8, p. 15; Lemma 4.18, pp. 65–66; BIP lines 2413–2421; EP lines 369–377

tests.statement: V=0 gives zero integral and rational testing modules.
For the model M=O[[H]] and Θ=O with trivial action, the testing module is O via augmentation; its rational version is L.
Replacing Θ by ϖΘ leaves the rational module unchanged, although the canonical integral lattice map is multiplication by ϖ.
For the model M=O/ϖ and Θ=O with trivial H, the testing module is zero; it does not recover the nonzero torsion module.
For M=O[[K]], [K:H]=n and dim_L V=r, Hom_H(M,V*) and Hom_K(M,(Ind_H^K V)*) both have L-dimension nr. Taking n=2 and r=1 gives 2 on both sides; forgetting cosets gives 1.
For H=K the induction comparison is the identity, with n=1 and both dimensions r.
M∞ is finite over R∞[[H]]; its testing quotient’s reducedness is the arithmetic assertion imported from the parent.

targets.name: Capture by smooth types
targets.statement: Use the type-theory supplier for the EP families: principal-series Vχ on a sufficiently small torsion-free Iwahori subgroup I_{n0}, and minimal-stratum V(α,θ) on H=U^{m+1}(𝔄) for an embedded degree-d extension E/F containing a minimal element, m sufficiently large that H is torsion free. In the principal family characters have pairwise separated conductors as in EP §3.3; in the supercuspidal family take all distinct isomorphism classes for all n>2m, v_E(α)=−n and θ∈C(m,α). Each family captures every compact projective over its H. Tensoring it with the nonzero fixed algebraic factor πalg(k)|_H preserves capture. Family members have finite fields of definition over L individually, interpreted through the imported coefficient-descent interface.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: Import the actual induced representations, hereditary-order filtration and simple-character intertwiners from the gap:minimal-stratum-types and gap:principal-series-types. Use EP Proposition 2.23 on the torsion-free compact p-adic analytic subgroup H: let (H_n) be a neighbourhood basis of open normal subgroups, with one uniform pro-p member H_n₀ such that for every integer j≥1 some H_n equals (H_n₀)^(p^j). For pairwise nonisomorphic smooth absolutely irreducible V_i, the growth Σ_i(dim V_i^{H_n})²∼[H:H_n] implies capture. Here ∼ means bounded above and below by positive constants, as used in EP. Principal-series counts are EP Lemma 3.10 and Proposition 3.11; simple-type dimensions and counts are Lemma 3.20 and Proposition 3.25, giving Proposition 3.26. Apply nonzero tensor stability to πalg(k). Restriction of the parent projective module to finite-index H remains projective.

tests.statement: For the principal-series family, dim Vχ grows as q^(n d(d−1)/2) and the number of characters as q^(nd), so the sum of squared dimensions grows as q^(nd²), matching [I_n₀:K_n₊₁].
For d=1 this becomes 1²·q^n=q^n; repeating just the trivial character cannot give the required q^n distinct classes.
The algebraic tensor factor has positive dimension. Tensoring with 0 yields no detecting maps and is excluded.

For H=ℤ_p² and the cyclic k[[H]]-module k[[ℤ_p]] acted on through the second factor, the filtration p^nℤ_p⊕p^(2n)ℤ_p gives coinvariant dimension p^(2n) and index p^(3n), whereas the dimension-ratio prediction is p^(3n/2). An arbitrary anisotropic filtration cannot replace the specified power-compatible one (EP Remark 2.19, pp. 348–349, EP lines 520–529).

targets.name: Fixed-centre algebraic density
targets.statement: Let 𝐆/ℚ_p be connected reductive and split over L, Z its centre and H⊆𝐆(ℚ_p) compact open. Let T≠0 be a finite-dimensional continuous L-representation of H whose central character restricts to δ:H∩Z(ℚ_p)→O×. If Π is an admissible unitary Banach representation that is a continuous H-equivariant direct summand of Cδ(H,L)^m, m≥1, then the images of Hom_H(T⊗ξ′,Π^la)⊗(T⊗ξ′), for ξ′ irreducible algebraic representations of (𝐆/Z)_L, span a dense subspace of Π^la. They also span a dense subspace of Π, using density of locally analytic vectors in an admissible Banach representation. All analytic vectors here are locally ℚ_p-analytic.
hypotheses: 𝐆/ℚ_p connected reductive and split over finite L, H compact open, T≠0 finite-dimensional continuous with central character δ, Π an admissible unitary summand of Cδ(H,L)^m.
targets.proofSketch: Use DPS Theorem 7.4 and Corollaries 7.5–7.6 for algebraic matrix coefficients on the compact open of the quotient by the centre. Tensor by T*; the projection formula Cδ(H,L)⊗T*≅C(H/(H∩Z),L)^{dim T} removes the central character. Pass to the continuous direct summand. Apply DPS Corollary 7.8 for density in Π^la. The PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp §0.1 analytic-vector-density theorem gives density in Π; this additional implication is explicit.

locator.where: DPS Theorem 7.4 and Corollaries 7.5–7.8, pp. 41–43; BIP proof of Lemma 6.7, p. 49; DPS lines 1981–1997

tests.statement: For the trivial reductive group 𝐆=H={1}, Π=L and T=L^r with r>0, evaluation Hom_L(T,L)⊗T→L sends e₁*⊗e₁ to 1, so its image is L. For T=0 it is 0.

For H=PGL₂(ℤ₂) in 𝐆=PGL₂ over ℚ₂, the centre is trivial and Π=C(H,L) is its own regular summand. The six indicators of H→PGL₂(𝔽₂)≅S₃ span a six-dimensional analytic subspace; indicators on finer open cosets approximate every continuous function uniformly.
For Π=0 the evaluation image and both target spaces are 0.

targets.name: Algebraic detection of projectives
targets.statement: For K=GL_d(O_F), let θ be an algebraic character of (Res_{F/ℚ_p}G_m)_L, with evaluation δ on Z∩K. If M is a nonzero projective in the category of compact O[[K]]-modules on which Z∩K acts by δ^{-1}, then Hom_cont,K(M,ξ*)≠0 for some irreducible algebraic ξ of (Res_{F/ℚ_p}GL_d)_L.
hypotheses: F/ℚ_p finite, L splits Res GL_d, θ algebraic, M≠0 projective pseudo-compact with central character δ⁻¹; no patching prime restriction.
targets.proofSketch: A compact fixed-centre projective is a product of indecomposable projectives. A nonzero factor is a summand of the fixed-centre completed regular module; its Banach dual is a nonzero summand of Cδ(K,L). The highest-weight classification in ReductiveGroups §10B supplies an algebraic T of central character θ, allowing arbitrary integer exponents at each embedding. This is not restricted to determinant powers. Fixed-centre evaluation density supplies ξ′ with a nonzero map T⊗ξ′→Π(M). Complete reducibility over L supplies an irreducible summand ξ with a nonzero map. Schikhof duality converts this to the asserted map M→ξ*. For a product, compose with the projection to the detected factor.

api.statement: For θ(z)=∏_σ σ(z)^(n_σ), there is an irreducible rational representation with this central character: at σ use dominant weight (n_σ,0,…,0) if n_σ≥0, and (0,…,0,n_σ) if n_σ<0. Each weight sum is n_σ.

locator.where: BIP Lemma 6.7, p. 49; BIP lines 2432–2446

tests.statement: For d=1 the representation is the character θ itself.
For d=2 a central exponent 1 is realized by the standard representation, highest weight (1,0); determinant powers have even exponent and miss it.
For d=2 a central exponent −1 is realized by the dual standard representation, highest weight (0,−1); (−1,0) would not be dominant.

layers.title: Faithfulness of the local deformation action

targets.name: Detection of local components
targets.statement: For every minimal prime 𝔭χ of R=R□_{ρ̄}, there is a minimal prime 𝔮 of R∞ with 𝔮∩R=𝔭χ and V(𝔮)⊆V(Ann_{R∞}M∞). More precisely, a crystalline determinant ψ restricting to χ on μ_{p∞}(F) and some algebraic ξ give a nonzero characteristic-zero fixed-ψ fibre of M∞(ξ); a point y of that fibre lies on such a component V(𝔮). No containment of the entire support of M∞(ξ) in one component is asserted.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: For the chosen χ, import the corrected crystalline-character lift interface to choose ψ lifting detρ̄ and realizing χ. The nonzero fixed-centre projective Mψ has an algebraic test ξ by Layer 3. Duality gives a nonzero fixed-ψ rational testing module. Its finite presentation over a characteristic-zero quotient of R∞ gives a closed point y. Every algebraic test is annihilated by Ann_{R∞}M∞, so y∈V(Ann M∞). The parent EP support theorem makes this closed set a union of irreducible components. Choose one such component through y; the algebraic-test closure form of EP Theorem 6.12 gives the same argument. At y, p is invertible; distinct determinant-torsion characters have distinct values, so its χ-component is unique. The component bijection of Layer 2 forces 𝔮∩R=𝔭χ. The proof only requires this chosen component through y.

locator.where: BIP proof of Theorem 6.8, p. 49; EP Theorem 6.12, pp. 369–370, imported through the parent; BIP lines 2448–2461

tests.statement: In Spec L[x,y]/(xy), the union of the two axes is not contained in either axis. The point (1,0) lies only on (y), while (0,0) lies on both; choose a component through the point.
For distinct χ and χ′ on μ_p(F), their values coincide modulo ϖ but are unequal in characteristic zero. A closed generic point therefore determines one χ, whereas a special-fibre point cannot.
If A has two components and the supported components are (χ,𝔭₁) for every χ, all local components are met while the components (χ,𝔭₂) need not be.

targets.name: Faithfulness of the local deformation action
targets.statement: For p∤2d and arbitrary continuous ρ̄ in the standing setup, the structural action R□_{ρ̄}→End_cont,O[[K]](M∞) is injective; equivalently Ann_{R□_{ρ̄}}M∞=0. This asserts faithfulness of the local ring, not of R∞.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: If a∈R kills M∞, its image lies in every minimal prime 𝔮 chosen by Layer 4 component detection. Contraction puts a in every minimal prime 𝔭χ of R. Their intersection is its nilradical. The local-ring supplier gives reducedness of R, hence a=0. Use the baseline annihilator criterion to express faithfulness. Descend from any coefficient enlargement by faithful flatness.

locator.where: BIP Theorem 6.8 and Remark 6.9, pp. 49–50; BIP lines 2447–2461

tests.statement: For B=O[[x]]/(x²), the intersection of its minimal primes is (x)≠0, with x²=0; component detection alone cannot give a zero annihilator without reducedness.
For a single geometrically integral auxiliary factor, the component pairs are just the χ, so this argument reaches every patched component.
For two auxiliary components, selecting one over each χ gives full local coverage but only half of the patched component pairs.

targets.name: Density from patched testing
targets.statement: Let R→R∞ be a continuous map of complete Noetherian local O-algebras with finite residue field with a continuous commuting action on the imported compact projective M∞, faithful over R. Let (V_i) capture M∞ on a fixed compact open H⊆K, and let N_i=M∞,H(Θ_i) be the finite integral tests. Suppose each B_i=R∞/Ann_{R∞}N_i is reduced and O-flat (the zero ring is allowed), and the image in Spec R of every closed point of Spec B_i[1/p] lies in a set Σ of arithmetic points. Then the vanishing ideal of Σ in R is zero and Σ is Zariski dense in Spec R. More generally, when the faithfulness assumption is dropped, its closure is V(Ann_R M∞) if, in addition, Σ⊆V(Ann_R M∞).
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: A scalar vanishing on Σ vanishes on every characteristic-zero closed point of B_i. Its generic fibre is Jacobson with finite residue extensions; reducedness and O-flatness give that the scalar is zero in B_i. Thus it kills N_i, hence kills every testing map by the dual-Hom comparison. Capture says its endomorphism on M∞ is zero. Capture gives vanishingIdeal(Σ)⊆Ann_R M∞. If Σ⊆V(Ann_R M∞), the reverse inclusion also holds; in the faithful case both are zero. Baseline zero-locus/closure gives the conclusion. This argument takes finite tests over R∞; it never assumes that M∞ is finite over R[[H]]. Equivalently EP Proposition 2.11 may be applied to R∞/Ann M∞ and then contracted.

locator.where: EP Lemmas 2.7, 2.10 and Proposition 2.11, pp. 344–345; Remark 2.13, pp. 345–346; BIP proof of Theorem 6.1, pp. 49–50; EP lines 320–399; BIP lines 2462–2476

tests.statement: For B=O[[x]]/(x²), every characteristic-zero point sends x to 0 but x≠0; reducedness is needed for ideal equality.
For B=O[[x]]/(ϖx), x≠0 vanishes in B[1/p]; O-flatness is needed even though B is reduced.
For the zero testing module N_i=0, Ann N_i=R∞ and B_i=0, whose spectrum is empty and vanishing ideal is the whole zero ring.
For R=O, M=O and the trivial test, the generic point has kernel 0 in O, so its closure is Spec O including (ϖ).

targets.name: Density of crystalline points
targets.statement: If p∤2d, then Σcris is Zariski dense in X□=Spec R□_{ρ̄}. The labelled regular weights vary; coefficients are allowed finite extensions of L.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: For every algebraic ξ, take the K-test M∞(ξ); these ξ capture the compact projective M∞. The parent crystalline specialisation theorem identifies its faithful quotient with a reduced O-flat union of components of the appropriate crystalline deformation ring, including the auxiliary factors. All characteristic-zero points map to Σcris. Apply Layer 5 testing density with Layer 4 faithfulness.

locator.where: BIP Theorem 6.1 and proof, pp. 46, 49–50; CEGGPS Lemma 4.18, pp. 65–66; BIP lines 2311–2312, 2462–2476

tests.statement: For d=1 this agrees with the algebraic-character interpolation from local class field theory.
For d=2,F=ℚ_p,p>2 it specializes to the known framed crystalline-density theorem; no claim at p=2 is made by this proof.

targets.name: Density of principal-series points
targets.statement: For p∤2d and every fixed regular labelled Hodge–Tate weight k, the potentially crystabelline subset Σprnc_k is Zariski dense in X□.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: Fix ξ=πalg(k) with the dual highest-weight convention in Layer 1. Restrict M∞ to the small Iwahori subgroup of EP §3.3. The principal-series smooth family, tensored with this fixed ξ, captures the restriction of M∞. Use EP Theorem 5.3 and its principal-series proof, with the type recognition of gap:principal-series-types and parent local–global compatibility: the faithful test quotients are reduced O-flat, and every characteristic-zero point is potentially crystabelline of weight k. The testing criterion and local faithfulness transfer the annihilator-supported statement to all X□.

locator.where: BIP Theorem 6.1 and proof, pp. 46, 50; EP proof of Theorem 5.1, pp. 363–364; Theorem 5.3 and proof, pp. 364–365; BIP lines 2477–2482; EP lines 1126–1164, 1202–1209

tests.statement: For d=1 at fixed weight, smooth characters of increasing conductor vary while the algebraic factor stays fixed; for ℤ_p the available finite-order characters of order dividing p^n number p^n.
Fixing weight and a single inertial type instead cuts out a generally proper potentially crystalline quotient.
The conclusion concerns Spec R, whereas fixed-weight points need not be dense in the rigid generic fibre (BIP Remark 6.10, p. 50).

targets.name: Density of supercuspidal points
targets.statement: For p∤2d and every fixed regular labelled weight k, Σspcd_k, with its unramified degree-d inducing extension and irreducible induced Weil representation, is Zariski dense in X□.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: Use E/F unramified of degree d and its EP §3.4 minimal-stratum family, tensored with the fixed ξ=πalg(k). Unramified E admits a minimal element. EP Proposition 3.19 recognizes these types, and local–global compatibility gives the reduced O-flat faithful quotients used in Theorem 5.3. For unramified E the corresponding Weil representation is irreducible character induction. Apply the capture criterion on the small hereditary-order subgroup, then contract by local faithfulness.

locator.where: BIP Theorem 6.1, p. 46; proof, p. 50; EP Proposition 3.19, p. 356; Theorem 5.3, pp. 364–365; BIP lines 2306–2312, 2477–2482; EP lines 824–843, 1202–1209

tests.statement: For d=1, E=F and the induction has dimension one; Σspcd_k=Σprnc_k=Σ_k.
An unramified degree-d extension has e=1, so the tame part of EP Proposition 3.19 applies.

targets.name: Density of benign points
targets.statement: For p∤2d, benign crystalline points with regular labelled weights varying are Zariski dense in X□.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: For each algebraic test quotient, benign points are dense in every component of its characteristic-zero support by CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility §5.2a. A local scalar vanishing on all benign points therefore vanishes on every reduced integral test quotient. Algebraic capture and local faithfulness give zero vanishing ideal, exactly as in crystalline density.

locator.where: BIP Remark 6.2, p. 46; EP Proposition 6.9 and its use preceding Lemma 6.11, p. 368; BIP lines 2313–2316; EP Proposition 6.9; EP lines 1320–1336

tests.statement: In rank one all eigenvalue-pair and refinement conditions are vacuous, so benign crystalline points are precisely crystalline points.
For rank two the eigenvalue ratio p^f is excluded: at f=1 and eigenvalues 1,p, the ratio is p. Regular weights alone do not imply benignness.
For a zero algebraic test the support is empty; its benign locus contributes no points. For a nonempty test, openness is relative to each crystalline component.

targets.name: Prescribed inertial type tests
targets.statement: For every inertial type τ (a finite-image inertia representation extending to W_F), choose the nonzero smooth K-type W=σ(τ) with CEGGPS N=0 recognition and a finite coefficient model. For each irreducible algebraic ξ let N_{ξ,τ}=M∞(ξ⊗W), using stable integral lattices for annihilators, and put Jτ=⋂_ξ Ann_R N_{ξ,τ} and Cτ=V(Jτ). Let Στ consist of potentially crystalline arithmetic points of type τ with arbitrary regular labelled weights, and Στ^patch be the images of closed generic points of the faithful test quotients. A zero representation W=0 is allowed only as a degenerate test of this construction, giving J=R and C=∅; it is never σ(τ).
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: Use the parent §5.2 type-specialised modules and contract their annihilators to R. Their faithful quotients are reduced and O-flat, so the Jacobson and integral-point interfaces identify Jτ with the vanishing ideal of Στ^patch. The recognition theorem identifies those points as potentially crystalline of type τ. Since σ(τ)≠0, algebraic capture tensor σ(τ) captures M∞, and §4.2 gives Jτ=Ann_R M∞=0.

api.statement: Jτ is radical and p-saturated, since each faithful test quotient is reduced and O-flat.
The type recognition theorem gives Στ^patch⊆Στ, including N=0.
The vanishing ideal of Στ^patch equals Jτ.
For every inertial type τ, Jτ=Ann_R M∞=0 and Cτ=X□.
For a degenerate W=0, every test is zero, J=R and C=∅.
Restricting the intersection to a single algebraic ξ gives its contracted testing support, which need not equal X□.

locator.where: BIP Remark 6.2, p. 46; CEGGPS Theorem 3.7, p. 41 and §3.13; EP Corollary 3.2, p. 351; BIP lines 2313–2314; CEGGPS lines 1651–1663; EP lines 618–621

tests.statement: For W=0, Ann_R(0)=R, so J=R and V(J)=∅; this distinguishes zero test data from any inertial type.
For trivial τ the construction contains all crystalline algebraic tests, and Jτ=0, Cτ=X□.
For d=1 and F=ℚ_p, type trivial with weight zero forces unramified inertia, cutting out a proper locus; ranging over the weights instead gives Cτ=X□.
For μ_{p∞}(F) cyclic of order p^a, a fixed rank-one type τ can be combined with algebraic powers σ(z)^n. As n runs modulo p^a, the restriction runs through all p^a determinant-torsion characters.

targets.name: Density for every prescribed inertial type
targets.statement: For p∤2d and every inertial type τ, the potentially crystalline points of type τ with regular labelled Hodge–Tate weights varying are Zariski dense in X□=Spec R□_{ρ̄}, allowing finite coefficient extensions.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: CEGGPS Theorem 3.7 gives σ(τ)≠0. The algebraic capture and nonzero tensor stability supplied in §3.1 apply with W=σ(τ). Parent §5.2 gives reduced O-flat faithful type quotients and recognition of their characteristic-zero points. Apply §5.1 and §4.2 to get Jτ=0 and density on all X□.

locator.where: BIP Remark 6.2, p. 46; EP Corollary 3.2, p. 351; BIP lines 2313–2314; EP lines 618–621; CEGGPS Theorem 3.7, p. 41

tests.statement: For d=1 the algebraic powers at a fixed τ meet every μ_{p∞}(F)-component, as computed in §6.2.
The degenerate W=0 family has no arithmetic points and J=R; it is excluded by σ(τ)≠0.
Fixing both τ and a single weight gives a potentially crystalline quotient, generally proper; this theorem varies the weights.

targets.name: Minimal-stratum supercuspidal points
targets.statement: Fix an embedded extension E/F of degree d containing an element minimal over F. Write e=e(E/F), v_E normalized and ϖ_F a uniformizer. Minimal means gcd(e,v_E(α))=1 and the residue of ϖ_F^{−v_E(α)}α^e generates k_E/k_F. Choose an O_F-basis of O_E to identify its lattice with O_F^d. Let 𝔄 be the hereditary order of End_F(E) preserving the chain (𝔭_E^i). For regular weight k, Σsc_{k,E} consists of potentially semistable points of that weight whose local Langlands representation is supercuspidal and contains a simple stratum [𝔄,n,0,α] with F[α]=E and α minimal, v_E(α)=−n<0. Simple strata, simple characters and their occurrence are imported from the smooth-representation owner. This predicate also covers wild E/F outside the range of the density theorem in §6.5.
hypotheses: F/ℚ_p finite, d≥1, E/F a degree-d extension admitting a minimal element; regular labelled weight k. No prime restriction is imposed on this definition.
targets.proofSketch: Apply the supplied minimal-stratum/type occurrence predicate to the local Langlands representation. The field embedding and lattice chain are specified up to conjugacy. The numerical minimality condition is the EP §3.4 input; it implies F[α]=E. The filtration and type constructors remain the supplier’s definitions; the chosen lattice puts U^{m+1}(𝔄) inside K. Use type recognition to see that such supercuspidal points have N=0. Character induction is available only under the extra tame hypothesis of EP Proposition 3.19.

api.statement: Changing the embedding E↪End_F(F^d) by conjugation gives the same point predicate.
Every point of this set is potentially crystalline, with N=0.
Membership is detected by occurrence of some V(α,θ) of the EP §3.4 family in the corresponding smooth representation, with the specified k.
For tame E/F the type condition is equivalent to the character-induction description with ψ|U_E^{m+1}=θ|U_E^{m+1}; no such equivalence is asserted for wild E.
Finite coefficient extension does not change the underlying arithmetic point predicate.

locator.where: EP Definition 3.12 and Example 3.15, p. 354; Proposition 3.19, p. 356; §5.3, p. 364; BIP Remark 6.2, p. 46; EP lines 753–843

tests.statement: For totally ramified E/F, a uniformizer α has v_E(α)=1 and gcd(e,1)=1, while k_E=k_F makes the residue-generation condition automatic. Its inverse has valuation −1 and is minimal as well.
For E/F unramified of degree d, a unit ξ with generating residue gives α=ϖ_F^(−n)ξ: e=1, gcd(1,−n)=1 and the required residue is ξ̄.

For F=ℚ_5, f(E/F)=2 and e(E/F)=6, the extension obtained from the unramified quadratic field and 5^(1/6) has degree 12. Sixth powers in 𝔽₂₅× form its subgroup of order 4, exactly 𝔽₅×, so it has no minimal element (EP Example 3.15).
For F=ℚ_3, d=3 and E=ℚ_3(3^(1/3)), e=3 and a uniformizer is minimal. The definition uses simple strata here; p divides 2d=6, so §6.5 gives no density claim for this wild instance.

targets.name: Density with a minimal-stratum inducing extension
targets.statement: Assume p∤2d. For every fixed regular weight k and every degree-d extension E/F containing a minimal element, Σsc_{k,E} is Zariski dense in X□. Since d=e(E/F)·f(E/F) and p∤d, every such E/F is tamely ramified. Equivalently these points have irreducible WD representation Ind_{W_E}^{W_F}ψ with ψ|U_E^{m+1}=θ|U_E^{m+1} for some EP minimal α of valuation −n, n>2m, and θ∈C(m,α), where m is chosen so U^{m+1}(𝔄) is torsion free. Every totally ramified degree-d extension is included.
hypotheses: Standing finite-extension arithmetic setup; p∤2d for assertions using M∞.
targets.proofSketch: Choose m as stated and the supplied V(α,θ) family. EP Lemma 3.16 supplies arbitrarily negative minimal elements from one such element. The family captures by §3.3 after tensoring with the nonzero fixed algebraic representation. EP Proposition 3.19 applies in its tame form to every E in this theorem, with the displayed character restriction. Parent §5.2 and the EP Theorem 5.3 argument identify reduced O-flat faithful quotients. Apply §5.1 and §4.2 to obtain density in X□.

tests.statement: For p=5,d=2 and E=ℚ_5(√5), e(E/F)=2,f(E/F)=1 and p∤2d=4; the uniformizer is minimal and the tame induced-character description applies.
For unramified E, e=1 and this recovers §5.4.
For the degree-12 extension over ℚ_5 in §6.4, 5∤24 but no minimal element exists; the minimal-element hypothesis is necessary.

suppliers.what: General GL_d(F) patched rings and M∞, fixed-centre projectivity, locally algebraic testing quotients, local–global compatibility, benign loci on every crystalline component and support as a union of components; capture requires gap:algebraic-capture.
Crystalline, potentially semistable and Weil–Deligne functors, coefficient change, labelled characters and the corrected crystalline-character lift interface.

Completed coefficient algebra and component pairs, framed local point functor, character ring, Hodge and inertial types, reduced O-flat potentially crystalline quotients and equidimensional fixed-type generic fibres; unrestricted components require gap:framed-ring-components.

Completed tensor products, Jacobson generic fibres with finite closed-point residue extensions, geometrically integral component pairs and reduced O-flat quotients detected by integral points; the two tensor refinements are declared gaps.
Schikhof duality, compact balanced tensors, qualified torsion-free biduality, admissible Banach–finite Iwasawa module anti-equivalence and locally ℚ_p-analytic vectors.
The general compact p-adic analytic group theorem that analytic vectors are dense in an admissible Banach representation; only this general foundational theorem is used.
Arithmetic Artin reciprocity, its geometric inverse, units and the torsion-free abelian Galois quotient, and Weil groups.
Complete reducibility in characteristic zero and rational simple representations of split reductive groups over L, with dominant highest weights and coefficient transport.

Smooth induction, Bernstein theory, shared Weil–Deligne objects and maximal distinguished cuspidal types built from simple strata and simple characters; the three finite-coefficient type extensions are declared separately.
Supercuspidal parameters, full Weil–Deligne correspondence and its identification with the classical geometric normalization, transported to CEGGPS r_p.
Continuous measures and the completed regular module on the pinned completed group algebra; the projective decomposition requires gap:projective-products.
Potential diagonalizability, component criteria and coefficient transport; the universal crystalline lift requires gap:pd-crystalline-lift.
Only the unmet gap:continuous-finite-index-induction contract is consumed; this supplier must be packaged before this roadmap can be packaged or ported.

gaps.title: framed ring components
gaps.needs: For every finite F/ℚ_p and residual ρ̄, R□ is reduced, O-flat and equidimensional, and after finite coefficient extension its minimal-prime quotients are exactly the determinant-torsion rings R□,χ, each a geometrically integral normal domain.
